narrative: Pearl's research side had a genuinely substantive day: @prlnet published a technical paper on GPU non-determinism (the same matrix multiplication produces different results across NVIDIA Ampere, Hopper and Lovelace due to architecture-specific behavior, not randomness), which drew organic engagement well beyond the usual noise — directly relevant since Pearl's useful-work PoW depends on verifiable GEMM results across heterogeneous hardware. Two GitHub repos also picked up after quiet stretches: the core repo shipped an Oyster CLI wallet UX fix, and the long-dormant PIPs repo restructured EIP-style with a new GitHub Pages docs site. Network difficulty continues easing (27.2M → 25.7M) with block time holding steady (~320-340s) — still reads as post-fork normalization. Bridge and market activity were unremarkable day-to-day. Spam-signal mention volume roughly halved from yesterday's peak (105, from 255).

social.summary: The standout item was @prlnet's technical paper on GPU non-determinism across NVIDIA GPU generations — organic replies called it "outstanding work" and highlighted independent verification as the real breakthrough, directly tying to Pearl's verifiable-compute PoW design. Templated pump-signal spam ("#Prl + 10%, join our telegram") continued but roughly halved from yesterday's peak. Pearlbridge's own account kept its dev-education cadence, including a scam warning (don't approve WPRL to an unfamiliar contract from a "bridging guide"). As always, the distinct "Perle Labs" project sharing the PRL ticker is unrelated and excluded.

sample_tweets.snippet: GPU non-determinism forced us to reverse-engineer arithmetic that modern AI hardware does not expose. The same matrix multiplication can produce different results across NVIDIA Ampere, Hopper and Lovelace GPUs.
Outstanding work. The most significant breakthrough isn't determinism itself, but independent verification.
If a "bridging guide" tells you to approve WPRL to some unfamiliar contract before you have even bridged anything, stop. That is not a step in the real flow.

incidents.summary: Pearl's July 1 MoE (mixture-of-experts) PoW extension had an economic-pricing bug: sparse expert-routed proofs were credited as full dense-difficulty work, letting miners claim outsized rewards without proportional real compute (not proof forgery, no PearlBridge custody impact, and DeFiLlama's hack database lists nothing for Pearl). Reported network hashrate rose from ~30 EH/s to 90+ EH/s over three weeks as this was exploited. The core team activated a dense-only PoW fork at mainnet height ~91,630 to shut off MoE crediting, with a same-day hotfix for a template-classification bug in the fork logic itself. Current chain height (91,737) is past the fork — the fix is live.

MinePRL, the canonical community pool tracked by this dashboard, is offline (site redirects visitors to prlscan.com); exact offline date within the past ~6 weeks is unconfirmed. Network hashrate and pool worker-count fields are null this snapshot pending a replacement public data source.
